clippings.speaker: Guillermo del Toro
clippings.quote: A good Bunraku artist moves the creature or character, but an excellent Bunraku artist fuses with the puppet, and that's what Doug does. … there's the rarest of the rare, which is a guy who can actually act and be an actor under make-up, and that's Doug Jones. He can do it.
clippings.title: Guillermo del Toro on The Shape of Water and Beautiful Monsters
clippings.context: Asked what makes Jones such a great monster actor, during an awards-season directors' panel.

clippings.speaker: Guillermo del Toro
clippings.quote: He came in and Doug was eating a bagel and sipping coffee from a foam cup, and Richard came to me and said, "What the fuck is this?! There's a guy in a fish suit! What are we doing here?!" … And then, I said, "Action!," and Doug instantly started acted. He became a creature that had never seen a bathtub and never said tiles.
clippings.title: Guillermo del Toro on The Shape of Water and Beautiful Monsters
clippings.context: Del Toro's anecdote about Richard Jenkins's first day shooting opposite Jones in the bathtub scene.

clippings.speaker: Guillermo del Toro
clippings.quote: It needed a human inside because of the nuance of the characters looking at one another. It needed a lot of things that only Doug can deliver.
clippings.title: On The Set Of 'The Shape Of Water' - Guillermo Del Toro Interview
clippings.context: On-set piece; del Toro explains why the Amphibian Man had to be a performer in a suit rather than a puppet.

clippings.speaker: Guillermo del Toro
clippings.quote: And Doug Jones is Doug Jones. Only he could have played this river god.
clippings.title: Shape of Water Is Guillermo del Toro's Passion Project
clippings.context: Press interview in which del Toro runs through what each lead actor brought to the film.

clippings.speaker: Doug Jones
clippings.quote: He's never let me play a human, and that's fine. He doesn't think of me as a human and I'm going to take that as a compliment because he loves his monsters so much. He has said, "I will always have a monster on my call sheet." … I've been 12 different characters for him now.
clippings.title: Meet Doug Jones, Guillermo del Toro's go-to monster man and star of 'The Shape of Water'
clippings.context: KPCC radio interview on The Frame about Jones's two decades playing del Toro's creatures.

clippings.speaker: Doug Jones
clippings.quote: I'll get a call usually late in the game. He's told me before when he's got something in development, "I've got something for you, but I'm not going to tell you about it because if we don't get to do the movie I don't want you to kill yourself."
clippings.title: Meet Doug Jones, Guillermo del Toro's go-to monster man and star of 'The Shape of Water'
clippings.context: Jones on how del Toro brings him onto projects.

clippings.speaker: Doug Jones
clippings.quote: And only Guillermo del Toro could fashion a movie together where the monster and a human form a romantic bond that the audience is actually rooting for. … I'm just so proud of Guillermo for having the vision and pushing forward with it
clippings.title: Interview [Part 2]: Doug Jones on Playing Saru in STAR TREK: DISCOVERY and Working with Guillermo del Toro on THE SHAPE OF WATER
clippings.context: Jones in a press interview ahead of The Shape of Water's release, which he calls his sixth film with del Toro.

notes: All sources are from the 2017-18 Shape of Water press cycle; earlier interviews (Hellboy, Pan's Labyrinth era) were not checked within budget.
